evals.name: morning-drink-pick
evals.prompt: /visualize Tea, coffee or an energy drink for a morning routine: compare them on caffeine, cost, crash and taste, and pick one.
evals.expected_output: A lead that names the pick, a lineup or matrix of the three options, the pick in the accent. A control only on a value the reader brings (servings, half-life); estimated prices stay static.

evals.name: letter-journey-overview
evals.prompt: /visualize How a letter gets from a mailbox to someone's door, step by step.
evals.expected_output: No options: a flow diagram as the main exhibit, the main path in the accent, claim headings. A stepper is allowed for states one after another.

evals.name: car-value-trend
evals.prompt: /visualize How a typical family car loses value over its first 10 years (invent plausible numbers, mark them as invented), and when the drop slows down.
evals.expected_output: Static: every input is invented, so no control. A trend chart of 10 years in series colors, the point where the drop slows as the main path, numbers marked as invented.

evals.name: retention-doc
evals.expected_output: How each cck store is bounded: every section and number of the doc placed or reported as left out, file names as sources. A control only on a setting the doc names (cleanupPeriodDays).

evals.name: slow-port-detection
evals.prompt: /visualize How the hub decides that an app's port is slow: {hub}/lib/port-health.js and the 'Slow ports' part of {hub}/CLAUDE.md. When is a port flagged, why does a busy app not count, and how long from the first slow probe to the badge?
evals.expected_output: Static exhibits for the rules (strike, busy app, 5 min window), plus a slider, toggle or stepper over the probe pattern; every number of port-health.js on the page.

evals.name: savings-growth
evals.prompt: /visualize How much a monthly saving of 200 grows over 30 years at different yearly interest rates, compounded monthly, and why starting 10 years earlier matters more than a higher rate.
evals.expected_output: A slider on the rate (or years, start age) that computes the chart again; the numbers in the text match the exhibit at its defaults; nothing runs while the reader does nothing.

evals.name: token-bucket
evals.prompt: /visualize How a token bucket absorbs bursts: a bucket of 10 tokens, refilled at 2 a second, against requests that arrive in bursts of 15 every 5 seconds. Which requests get rejected, and what bucket size would let every burst through?
evals.expected_output: Controls for bucket size and refill rate. The default rejects 5 requests of each burst. No bucket size is enough at 2 a second: 5 s refills only 10 tokens, so a bucket of 15 passes the first burst and then rejects 5 each time; every burst passes only with a refill of at least 3 a second and a bucket of at least 15.
